Question Choices: What general shape does a normal distribution have?
Hints: The graph has one central peak.|Both tails taper away from the center.
Solution: A normal density is a symmetric bell-shaped curve with one peak at its mean. Its tails approach the horizontal axis in both directions. A roughly bell-shaped data plot may suggest, but does not by itself prove, a normal model.

Question Choices: A normal distribution is symmetric about which value?
Hints: The center is also the median and mode.|The two halves mirror each other.
Solution: The normal curve is symmetric about the mean. Its mean, median and mode coincide, so the two halves mirror each other around that central value.

Question Choices: About what percent of normally distributed data lie within 1 standard deviation of the mean?
Hints: Use the first part of the empirical rule.|Recall the 68-95-99.7 pattern.
Solution: For a normal distribution, the empirical rule places approximately 68%, 95% and 99.7% within 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations, respectively. Thus within 1 standard deviations on either side of the mean is about 68%. These are approximations, not universal percentages for all distributions.

Solution: For a normal distribution, the empirical rule places approximately 68%, 95% and 99.7% within 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations, respectively. Thus within 2 standard deviations on either side of the mean is about 95%. These are approximations, not universal percentages for all distributions.

Question Choices: About what percent of normally distributed data lie within 3 standard deviations of the mean?
Hints: Use the third part of the empirical rule.|Nearly all values are within three standard deviations.
Solution: For a normal distribution, the empirical rule places approximately 68%, 95% and 99.7% within 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations, respectively. Thus within 3 standard deviations on either side of the mean is about 99.7%. These are approximations, not universal percentages for all distributions.

Question Choices: A normal distribution has mean 70 and standard deviation 5. What interval is within 1 standard deviation? Enter the lower value then the upper value.
Hints: Subtract and add one standard deviation.|Compute 70-5 and 70+5.
Solution: The interval is mean plus or minus 1 standard deviation: 70-1(5)=65 and 70+1(5)=75. Enter the lower endpoint then the upper endpoint. Both endpoints are one standard deviation from the mean.

Question Choices: A normal distribution has mean 50 and standard deviation 4. What value is 2 standard deviations above the mean?
Solution: Two standard deviations are 2(4)=8. Above the mean means add, so the value is 50+8=58. Checking gives (58-50)/4=2.

Question Choices: What percent of a symmetric normal distribution lies above its mean?
Hints: The mean divides the symmetric curve into equal halves.|Half the area lies on each side.
Solution: A normal distribution is symmetric about its mean and has total area 1. Each half has area 1/2, so 50% lies above the mean. A single point at the mean has zero probability in this continuous model.

Question Choices: Two normal distributions have the same mean. Which one is wider: the one with larger or smaller standard deviation?
Question Answers: larger standard deviation|the one with larger standard deviation|larger
Hints: Standard deviation measures spread.|More spread produces a flatter wider curve.
Solution: With the same mean, a larger positive standard deviation spreads the normal density farther horizontally. Its peak is correspondingly lower so total area remains 1. Thus the larger-standard-deviation curve is wider.

Question Choices: A value below the mean has a positive or negative z-score? Assume a positive standard deviation.
Hints: The z-score measures signed distance from the mean.|Below the mean makes the numerator x-mean negative.
Solution: Using z=(value-mean)/standard deviation, a value below the mean gives a negative numerator. The standard deviation is positive, so z is negative.
